script: "Almost blinded myself—my eyes betrayed me after 20 years of neglect, and it got worse…". I was a hermit, living solo, no friends, no doctor visits, no eye exam for years. Then I moved halfway across the country to live with my girlfriend—now wife—and a friend. The first thing I noticed: my eyes were screaming. I'd been wearing two‑week disposables for over a year, just pulling them out at night, cleaning them, pretending it was fine because the redness was "allergies." (Micro‑hook: I was basically a walking eye‑infection.) After the move, I decided to finally get my life together and book an eye appointment. My partner got new glasses; I got my own appointment same day. She came back from the waiting room saying the optometrist was "so chill, like a dad at a barbecue." (Micro‑hook: the doc looked like Chuck Norris, no joke.) When I walked into the exam room, he was that Chuck Norris vibe—broad shoulders, intense stare. He asked me to pull my lenses out. I gave him my best guess on how long I'd worn them—like, "maybe six months?" He didn't smile. He asked, "Has anyone talked to you about vessel growth in your corneas?" I said no. He left the room for a minute, then returned with a diagram of an eye. He explained that my corneas needed oxygen from the air, but the lenses had been on so long and dirty that my corneas stopped breathing. The body's workaround? Growing blood vessels where they shouldn't be. (Stakes: my vision, my future, my sanity.) I was literally terrified. He said the lenses I'd been using were the worst he'd seen in his career, and that if I'd waited longer, I'd be permanently blinded. He drew lines across my pupil to show the vessels. He warned that unless I switched to the most breathable lenses—like the best of the best—those vessels would stay. He was stern, not yelling, but the vibe was, "you're in danger, bestie." (Tension wave: I could feel my heart racing.) I left the office with new lenses, but by the time they ran out, I had a job again—no benefits, no insurance. I thought, "Fine, I'll just go back to glasses." And that's what I do now. Every new optometrist sees the same shriveled‑up vessels and gets all excited. I keep them in the rearview of my life. (Clarity: I am not a health guru, but I've learned to check my eyes regularly.) TL;DR: I wore a pair of disposable contacts for over a year, got lectured by a doc who looked like Chuck Norris, learned my corneas were growing blood vessels, and now I live with glasses and yearly eye check‑ups. (PS: I finally booked an ortho for my old ankle injury—hope that's not another drama.)
